body:
## Summary

Add a first-class, engine-neutral download manager that can configure a persistent destination, observe automated **and manual** downloads, wait for completion, apply a safe name, avoid duplicate saves, validate the artifact, and expose failures.

This should work consistently through `launchBrowser()`, `connectBrowser()`, and `launchRealBrowser()` without requiring raw Playwright/Puppeteer events, CDP commands, or polling the operating-system Downloads folder.

## Current gap (reviewed against JavaScript 0.17.2 / current `main`)

There is no download API or documented download option in the JavaScript, Python, or Rust public surface. In JavaScript specifically:

- `launchBrowser()` does not accept or forward `downloadsPath`/a portable equivalent;
- the launch-option builders drop unknown options;
- the commander has no `onDownload`, `waitForDownload`, or download-and-save helper;
- attached/real-browser sessions do not configure a persistent download destination;
- `browser-commander/tests` cannot retain downloads as structured artifacts.

Current source references:

- [`launchBrowser()` accepts a fixed set of options and exposes no download configuration](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/blob/90a53ff11581d243fbd963593ec0fd7d33efd1b1/js/src/browser/launcher.js#L17-L52)
- [the Playwright/Puppeteer option builders expose no download destination](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/blob/90a53ff11581d243fbd963593ec0fd7d33efd1b1/js/src/browser/launch-options.js#L59-L132)
- [the public API exports no download lifecycle helper](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/blob/90a53ff11581d243fbd963593ec0fd7d33efd1b1/js/src/exports.js)

Raw engine defaults are surprising for application automation: a Playwright download may live in an engine-managed temporary directory and be deleted when its context closes. A visible browser can show a successful entry in its download UI while no suitably named file is present where the user expects it.

Downstream code consequently has to combine a page `download` listener, a listener armed before the click, `saveAs`, CDP download behavior for attached browsers, collision-safe naming, content validation, deduplication, and sometimes filesystem polling. That is generic browser lifecycle work and belongs in Browser Commander.

## Proposed API

Exact names are open; one possible shape is:

```js
const { browser, page, downloads } = await launchRealBrowser({
  engine: 'playwright',
  downloads: {
    directory: 'user-downloads', // 'temporary' | absolute path
    persist: true,
    conflict: 'rename', // 'overwrite' | 'error'
  },
});

downloads.on('completed', (artifact) => {
  console.log(artifact.path, artifact.suggestedFilename, artifact.mimeType);
});

const artifact = await downloads.capture({
  action: () => commander.click({ selector: '#download' }),
  filename: 'report.pdf',
  timeout: 20_000,
  validate: ({ bytes, mimeType }) =>
    mimeType === 'application/pdf' && bytes.subarray(0, 5).toString() === '%PDF-',
});
```

Equivalent functionality should be available on an already-created commander/context, for example `configureDownloads()` or `commander.downloads`.

## Required behavior

### Configuration and persistence

- Support an explicit absolute directory, a cross-platform `user-downloads` preset, and engine-managed `temporary` mode.
- Create the directory when requested and report permission/configuration failures before the first download.
- Persist completed files beyond page/context/browser closure when `persist` is enabled.
- For CDP-attached Chromium, configure download behavior internally where the selected engine does not expose sufficient behavior.
- Do not silently expose a user's default browser profile or weaken the dedicated-profile guarantees already implemented by `launchRealBrowser()`.

### One lifecycle for automated and manual downloads

- Observe downloads initiated by Browser Commander actions, page JavaScript/blob URLs, navigation, and a human clicking in a visible attached browser.
- Arm capture before the triggering action so fast downloads cannot race the listener.
- Emit `started`, `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled` with stable IDs.
- Surface engine errors and cancellation reasons; a download UI entry is not completion evidence.

### Safe artifact handling

- Preserve both the server/engine suggested name and the final saved name.
- Allow a caller-provided naming callback; sanitize path separators/control characters and prevent traversal.
- Handle names with no extension (including UUID-like names) using declared/detected MIME type when possible.
- Resolve collisions deterministically (`name (2).pdf`, overwrite, or error).
- Save to a temporary partial file and atomically rename only after completion/validation.
- Deduplicate the same engine download seen by a global listener and an awaited `capture()` call.
- Return useful metadata: final path, suggested name, URL (redactable), MIME type, byte count, checksum, timestamps, and engine failure.

## Privacy and security

- Download paths and URLs may contain sensitive information; integrate with the proposed trace redaction policy and logging controls.
- Default to no response-body logging and never log file contents.
- Refuse traversal, unsafe absolute names supplied by the page, and writes outside the configured root.
- Use owner-only permissions where the platform supports them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `launchBrowser()`, `connectBrowser()`, and `launchRealBrowser()` expose the same download configuration and manager shape.
- [ ] Playwright and Puppeteer tests cover browser-click, JavaScript/blob, and navigation downloads.
- [ ] A visible CDP-attached browser's manually initiated download is observed and persisted.
- [ ] A completed download remains after context/browser closure.
- [ ] A bare UUID filename with PDF content can be saved under a caller-selected `.pdf` name and validated.
- [ ] Fast downloads cannot race registration; failed/cancelled downloads never return success.
- [ ] Global observation plus `capture()` does not save or emit the same download twice.
- [ ] Filename collision, traversal, invalid-content, unwritable-directory, timeout, and partial-file cleanup cases are tested.
- [ ] `browser-commander/tests` can retain downloads in its artifact directory and a session trace can reference them without embedding contents by default.
- [ ] The API and behavior are documented in the cross-language parity matrix; unsupported engine limitations are explicit rather than silently ignored.

## Related work

- #39 provides raw-page access, which is the current escape hatch but should not be required for a core browser artifact lifecycle.
- #66 and #68 added CDP attach and real-browser launch; managed downloads need to behave the same in those modes.
title: Add managed persistent downloads across launch, attach, and real-browser sessions
